title: Embrace high clock frequency alongside traditional high-IPC approach
decision: Adopt a high-frequency (speed-demon) design philosophy in addition to the traditional high-IPC (brainiac) approach for IBM UNIX systems
alternatives_or_rejected: Pure brainiac (complex design prioritizing higher instructions-per-cycle at lower frequency), which IBM UNIX systems had traditionally followed
rationale: To maintain a leadership position and deliver best-of-breed operating frequencies while still pursuing complex superscalar out-of-order design; system designed so bus frequencies scale with processor frequency to preserve balance as technology improves
outcome: POWER4 introduced at 1.1 GHz and 1.3 GHz, surpassing other 64-bit microprocessors in key benchmarks; long pipeline mitigated by heavy investment in multilevel branch prediction
quote_as_recalled: In the ongoing debate between the “speed demons” (high clock rate) and the “braniacs” ... IBM opted to also embrace the speed-demon approach.
weakest_point: Exact wording of the full quote fragment may have minor punctuation variation

title: RAS philosophy: eliminate outages and convert checkstops to recoverable interrupts
where_in_paper: Guiding principles (Leadership in reliability, availability, and serviceability)
decision: Require an approach that eliminates outages, provides redundancy where errors cannot be eliminated, and transforms hard machine stops (checkstops) into synchronous machine interrupts to software whenever possible
alternatives_or_rejected: Achieving high reliability merely by choosing reliable parts and incorporating ECC into major arrays
rationale: Servers have evolved toward continuous operation; high levels of reliability cannot be achieved only by reliable parts and ECC; system must circumvent problems if possible
outcome: RAS attributes previously seen only in mainframes designed into POWER4 systems (detailed further in companion paper by Bossen et al.)
quote_as_recalled: we accepted the principle that one does not achieve high levels of reliability only by choosing reliable parts and incorporating error-correction-code (ECC) logic into major arrays.
weakest_point: Precise length of the quoted fragment

title: Full-system design and distributed-switch interconnect for scalable SMP
where_in_paper: Introduction and Guiding principles (Full-system design approach); later interconnect discussion
decision: Design the entire system together (processor, packaging, memory, I/O) from the outset and use a new distributed-switch interconnect topology to form SMPs up to 32-way
rationale: A new high-performance processor needs a new subsystem to feed it effectively; marriage of process technology, packaging and microarchitecture allows software to exploit them; interconnect appears bus-like to a chip but switch-like to a module and is new to the industry
outcome: Four chips form an 8-way MCM; four MCMs form a 32-way SMP; buses scale with processor frequency so system balance is maintained as frequency rises
quote_as_recalled: The interconnect topology, referred to as a distributed switch, is new to the industry.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly contrasts against a pure bus or pure crossbar alternative

title: Dual cores sharing on-chip unified L2 via CIU crossbar
decision: Place two identical processor cores on one chip sharing a unified second-level cache through a core interface unit (CIU) implemented as a crossbar among three autonomous L2 controllers
rationale: SMP optimization principle: large number of transistors used to improve total system performance in multitasking server environments; provides two-way SMP model to software on a single chip
outcome: Each L2 controller can feed 32 bytes per cycle concurrently; chip contains 174 million transistors; four chips packaged on one module yield an 8-way SMP
quote_as_recalled: The design features two processors on one chip; ... The two processors share a unified second-level cache ... through a core interface unit (CIU)
weakest_point: Exact page of the logical-view figure description

title: Binary compatibility and single design for both commercial and technical workloads
where_in_paper: Guiding principles (Binary compatibility; Balanced technical and commercial performance)
decision: Maintain absolute binary compatibility for 32-bit and 64-bit applications with prior PowerPC and PowerPC AS systems, and use a single design addressing both technical (high-bandwidth) and commercial (data-sharing/SMP) requirements
alternatives_or_rejected: Changing the architecture (rejected because internal task forces found no technical impediment to scaling PowerPC to higher frequencies)
rationale: Keep customers’ software investment intact; satisfy high-performance computing bandwidth demands together with commercial data-sharing and SMP scaling needs so that one design serves both pSeries and iSeries
outcome: POWER4 implements and extends the 64-bit PowerPC Architecture in a compatible manner; first used in pSeries, later staged into iSeries
quote_as_recalled: With no technical reason to change, in order to keep our customers software investment intact, we accepted the absolute requirement of maintaining binary compatibility
weakest_point: Whether the paper lists any specific rejected architectural change beyond the general statement
